Hi Emma — great conversation earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap + a couple of targeted asks so we can line up the right POC shape and the accompanying security evidence.

Recap (from our call)
- Primary goal: ingest and index PHI-backed clinical notes for internal clinician tools (no public-facing UI).
- Preference: strong tilt toward Private VPC if we can meet BYOK + private control plane requirements, but team is open to a Dedicated start if that shortens timeline.
- Hard constraints: no egress of raw customer data outside your VPC without explicit written approval; audit logs retained for 7 years; KMS secrets under customer control.

Asks / next steps
1) Can you confirm the minimal set of isolation controls that would force a Private VPC decision vs something we can accept on Dedicated for initial pilot? (e.g., BYOK required at go/no-go, control plane residency, subnet restrictions)
2) Please share the security questionnaire and any encryption/BYOK policy excerpts we should validate.
3) Tentative next call: technical deep-dive with our infra lead (Connor) — propose Wed 6/16 10am PT. Good for you?

Attached is a short checklist I drafted (redwood-dedicated-vs-vpc-checklist.pdf) to seed the discussion — it lists concrete items (control plane residency, KMS signer/rotation, egress rules, logging endpoints).

I'll loop in Marissa to sketch pricing paths (Dedicated vs Private ramp), and Connor for Ops-level feasibility.

Thanks — Diego

Diego — thanks for the summary, that matches our notes. A few clarifications from security/ops: 

1) BYOK is a gating requirement for production if we are storing PHI-derived model state or long-term embeddings. For an initial proof-of-concept (2-6 weeks), we are willing to accept a Dedicated pool with customer-dedicated nodes (no multi-tenant mixing) provided:
   - KMS keys are customer-managed and access is auditable;
   - Data egress to Redwood-managed storage is encrypted and blocked from any external services;
   - Audit logs (API + host-level) are sent to our Splunk tenant via secure forwarders.

2) For long-term deployment, we will require Private VPC with a private control plane (control plane traffic must remain inside our VPC or over an agreed peering link).

3) Timeline: we have an internal security review July 2 — would like any SOC2 / pen test summaries by then. I'll send our formal questionnaire (and a sample NDA redline) by EOD tomorrow.

On Wed 6/16 10am PT — yes, that works for Connor and me.

Best,
Emma Li
Director of Cloud Security, Medisafe Health

Diego / Marissa — quick ops notes ahead of the Wed deep-dive. Short answers:

1) Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated nodes) for POC
   - Feasible: yes. We can allocate a tenant-isolated set of nodes. BYOK: we support customer-managed KMS keys for disk and object encryption via our existing KMS bindings (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). Caveat: for short-term Dedicated POC we rely on our control plane for orchestration; keys can be customer-owned but control-plane logs will exist in Redwood unless we toggle private control plane.

2) Private control plane (customer VPC)
   - Supported regions: us-west-2, us-east-1 today. Additional regions require region provisioning (4-8 week lead time).
   - Lead time to stand up private control plane: typically 2-4 weeks in an existing account with completed network approvals.

3) Networking / peering
   - Minimal egress CIDRs we use: 34.216.0.0/14, 52.12.0.0/14 (these are the management/outbound ranges for the nodes). For peering we can do VPC peering or private link depending on the cloud provider.

4) Logging / audit exports
   - Splunk forwarder: supported via secure syslog endpoint or S3 bucket push.
   - Audit log retention: default 30 days on Redwood; can configure export to your S3 with lifecycle rules (we recommend at least 7 years if you need it).

5) PHI-handling callouts
   - KV cache: ephemeral by default between requests but persists for model session duration; we can enable guaranteed eviction and no-disk-backup for PII-sensitive paths.
   - Background snapshots: disabled on customer-dedicated node groups by request; if enabled, they are encrypted with customer KMS.

I'll attach the ops checklist and a small network diagram stub for the Wed call. Connor
